raw:
{
  "need": "Identity",
  "secondary": { "name": "Autonomy" },
  "read": "Your kid is publicly planting a flag about who they are becoming, and doing it at the dinner table means they wanted you to hear it. This is less about church and more about the urgent developmental work of figuring out what they actually believe versus what they were handed. The status angle: they need you to take their inner life seriously, not dismiss it as a phase or a rebellion.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Lay down the law that church attendance is not optional in this house, because you are the parent and these are your family values — which turns a values conversation into a power struggle and teaches them that faith is something imposed on them, not something they own." },
  "mentorMove": "Keep the expectation of shared family practice on the table while opening a genuine conversation about what they actually think and feel. You are not negotiating your values, but you are treating their emerging beliefs as worth a real conversation, which is the only thing that could ever matter in the long run.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "What we do as a family together, including how we practice faith, is something we figure out together, not something one person opts out of at dinner.",
    "Your honest questions and doubts about belief deserve a serious conversation, and you deserve to be heard, not just overruled."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How participation looks can be negotiated: sitting quietly, coming to some services but not all, talking privately with a pastor or faith leader they choose, or exploring their questions in another format.",
    "The timeline for resolution does not have to be tonight — this conversation can unfold over weeks if you both stay in it honestly."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 3, "label": "Collaboration" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "I am really glad you said that out loud instead of just going quiet on me. That took guts, and I want you to know I am not going to bite your head off." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "I do want to understand what is actually going on for you. Is it something specific that happened, or is it more like something you have been sitting with for a while? Because those are pretty different things and I want to hear the real one." },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is where I am: I am not going to pretend I do not care about this, because I do, and you already knew that. But I also do not want you going through the motions and resenting every minute of it, because that helps nobody. So let us figure out what this actually looks like. What would feel like it honored your questions without us just walking away from something that matters to our family?" },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I am holding on to this because I have high standards for our family and for you, and I genuinely believe you are someone who can wrestle with hard questions and come out with something real on the other side. That is not nothing. So we are not done with this conversation, but I am in it with you, not against you." }
  ],
  "longGame": "The kids who stay connected to faith, or who come back to it, or who land somewhere meaningful even if it looks different than what you hoped, are almost always the ones whose parents took their doubts seriously instead of shutting them down. Stay curious about their inner life over the next months, not just compliant about Sunday morning."
}
situation: My kid announced at dinner they are done with church and are not going anymore.
